questions.stem: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university sports facilities should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
In my view, university sports facilities should be opened to the public rather than kept behind closed gates. In the following paragraphs I will give my reasons.

To begin with, these facilities are usually built with public funding, yet they stand empty on weekends and holidays. Opening them turns a wasted resource into a shared benefit for taxpayers. What is more, many communities lack affordable places to exercise, so free access to a campus track or gym would clearly improve residents' health. Admittedly, some people worry about campus safety and extra costs. Nevertheless, these problems can be eased by fixed opening hours, an entry registration and a small fee.

To sum up, I firmly believe that universities should open their sports facilities to the public. It is advisable that they first set up proper management, so that both students and residents can enjoy the resource in harmony.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: 1 A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird.

The flight from Palm Beach International Airport to LaGuardia Airport turned around just minutes after takeoff following the strike. 2 No injuries were reported on the plane, and the flight took off once again 7.5 hours after the first attempt.
"It was like a split second of panic…that resulted in this nervous reaction on the plane," said passenger Brian Healy.
"There was total quiet, and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop." An email from JetBlue read, "Our team is working to accommodate customers on later flights."

questions.stem: What do we learn about the JetBlue Airlines flight from the news report?

options.text: It hit a bird shortly after takeoff.
Its crew members went on strike.
It narrowly escaped a plane crash when turning around.
Its captain got slightly injured during the forced landing.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird.信号：新闻首句即事件核心 。答案就在录音第一句 was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird：新闻报道往往开…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：Its crew members went on strike 说机组罢工，录音通篇只字未提任何罢工，返航原因明确是撞鸟，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：It narrowly escaped a plane crash when turning around 盗用了录音里真出现的 turn around（返航）来制造熟悉感，但录音只说返航降落、明说 No injuries were reported，根本没提 "险些坠机"，是把普通返航夸大成濒临坠机。 借用原文：No injuries were reported on the plane
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：Its captain got slightly injured during the forced landing 借用了录音真有的 forced to turn around and land（被迫降落）来骗耳朵，但录音紧接着明说 No injuries were reported on the plane——没有任何人受伤，更没说机长受伤，与原文正好相反。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（after the plane struck a bird ↔ It hit a bird struck 换成 hit）

questions.evidenceText: A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird.

questions.stem: How did the passengers feel when the plane came to a stop, according to Brian Healy?
questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P2）："There was total quiet, and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop."信号：题干时间词对准原文 。录音里 there was relief when the plane came to a stop 这句的时间状语 when the plane came to a stop 与题干一字不差，…

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：Panic 盗用了录音真说过的 a split second of panic，但那是描述事发瞬间（split second）的情绪，不是题干问的 "飞机停稳时"，时间点错位。 借用原文：this nervous reaction on the plane
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：Nervous 盗用了录音的 this nervous reaction on the plane，但那形容的是事件过程中的紧张反应，同样不是 "飞机停稳时" 的感受，时间点不符。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：Contented（满足）和正确项 relief 意思相近，是赌你分不清两个正面情绪词，但录音从头到尾只说了 relief，从没出现 "满足" 这层意思，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（there was relief ↔ Relieved 名词relief转形容词Relieved）

questions.evidenceText: "There was total quiet, and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop."

transcript.text: A deadly snake, which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time. The poisonous snake forced the closure of the attraction last week when staff noticed the disappearance.
transcript.zh: 一条致命的毒蛇在从动物园逃脱后终于被追踪到,却第二次溜走了。上周当工作人员注意到这条毒蛇失踪时,它迫使该景点关闭。

transcript.text: After six days of desperate searching, he was eventually found and placed in a supposedly secure area. But it seems the animal is no fan of the zoo, because yet again he is out on the loose. The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo but has already been frustrating its staff. The staff believe he squeezed himself out of a gap located around new energy-saving bulbs installed inside the snake house. He was only found the first time around because staff brought in a special machine to trace him inside a wall opening.
transcript.zh: 经过六天的拼命搜寻,它最终被找到并被安置在一个据称安全的区域。但这只动物似乎并不喜欢这家动物园,因为它再次逃脱了。这条蛇是动物园相对较新的成员,但已经让工作人员感到沮丧。工作人员认为它是从蛇舍内安装的新型节能灯泡周围的缝隙中挤出去的。它第一次被找到是因为工作人员带来了一台特殊的机器,在墙壁开口内追踪到了它。

transcript.text: This kind of snake is one of the most deadly and poisonous in the wild, and they can range from 3 to 5 meters in length.
transcript.zh: 这种蛇是野外最致命、毒性最强的蛇类之一,体长可达3至5米。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the deadly snake from the news report?

options.text: He is now kept in a secure area.
He has escaped the zoo once again.
He has been caught a second time.
He finally disappeared six days ago.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A deadly snake, which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time.信号：开篇首句即落点 。新闻的核心事实常压在第一句。这里 has slipped away for the second time（第二次溜走了）就是承载答案的信号句——它点明这条蛇"再次逃跑"这一最新状态。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确实念到 placed in a supposedly secure area（被放进所谓安全区域），但紧接着就是 yet again he is out on the loose——它早跑出来了。A 盗用 secure area 这个原词，描述的却是已被推翻的"上一个阶段"状态，不是它"现在"的状况。 借用原文：tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：录音里确有 tracked down 和 found（被找到/被抓）以及 second time 的字眼，C 用 caught a second time 把这些原词拼起来。但 second time 在录音里是修饰"逃跑"的（slipped away for the second time），抓只发生过一次。C 把动作方向从"逃"偷换成"抓"，与原文相反。 借用原文：After six days of desperate searching
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音的 After six days of desperate searching（搜寻了六天）里确有 six days，D 便拿 six days ago 来骗。但六天指的是"工作人员搜寻它花的时长"，不是它"六天前消失"；而且它现在是又跑了、不是"finally disappeared（终于消失）"。数字对得上、事却对不上。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（has slipped away for the second time ↔ has escaped the zoo once again slip away=escape，second time=once again）

questions.evidenceText: A deadly snake, which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time.

questions.stem: How have the zoo staff been feeling about the snake?
questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P2）：The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo but has already been frustrating its staff.信号：情绪动词 frustrating 。答案信号就是那个直接表达感受的词 frustrating its staff（让工作人员受挫/懊恼）。态度题的落点往往就是这样一个带感情色彩的形容词或动词，听到它就锁定。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音里 he squeezed himself out of a gap（蛇把自己挤出缝隙）确有 squeezed，A 就拿这个原词来骗。但 squeezed 讲的是蛇"怎么逃出去的"动作，根本不是工作人员的"感受"，与题目问的 feeling 完全是两码事。 借用原文：has already been frustrating its staff
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：这条蛇虽 deadly（致命），但录音从没说工作人员"感到受威胁"。Threatened 是顺着"毒蛇危险"自行脑补出来的情绪，录音里并无对应的词，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：Disappointed（失望）与正确的 Frustrated（受挫/懊恼）都是负面情绪、含义相邻，最难切开。但录音明明白白念的是 frustrating，不是 disappointing。C 用一个意思相近却并非原文的情绪词来顶替，差在"不是录音说的那个词"。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（has already been frustrating its staff ↔ Frustrated 主动 frustrating→被动 frustrated）

questions.evidenceText: The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo but has already been frustrating its staff.

transcript.text: Electric bikes have been the craze in downtown Jacksonville since they were first introduced earlier this month as a one-year pilot program. But they're leading to safety concerns, mainly at night when some riders don't follow the rules of the road.
transcript.zh: 自本月早些时候作为为期一年的试点项目首次引入以来,电动自行车在杰克逊维尔市中心引发了热潮。但它们引发了安全担忧,主要是在夜间,一些骑行者不遵守交通规则。

transcript.text: As the night goes on, groups of riders are often seen traveling in just about every direction in the streets and on pedestrian paths. That is increasing the probability of dangerous accidents.
transcript.zh: 随着夜幕降临,经常可以看到成群的骑行者在街道和人行道上几乎朝着各个方向行驶。这增加了发生危险事故的可能性。

transcript.text: Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile. That means no running red lights or traveling in the opposite direction of traffic on one-way streets.
transcript.zh: 电动自行车骑行者必须遵守与驾驶汽车时相同的所有规则。这意味着不能闯红灯,也不能在单行道上逆向行驶。

transcript.text: City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown. And she's aware of the concerns. Cumber said, "People can have fun, but both drivers and riders are responsible for paying attention while on the road. And never assume the driver is going to stop or see you."
transcript.zh: 市议会成员Anna Cumber在将电动自行车引入杰克逊维尔以为市中心注入新活力方面发挥了重要作用。她也意识到了这些担忧。Cumber说:"人们可以享受乐趣,但驾驶员和骑行者都有责任在路上保持注意力。永远不要假设驾驶员会停车或看到你。"

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?

options.text: It is condemned as a crazy idea.
It is enriching the city's night life.
It is questioned by local residents.
It is giving rise to safety concerns.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：But they're leading to safety concerns, mainly at night when some riders don't follow the rules of the road.信号：转折 But 之后才是真意 。答案藏在转折词后面：第 1 段先说电动车很火 Electric bikes have been the craze，紧接一个 But they're leading to safety …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音说电动车 have been the craze（很火爆、风靡），A 项 condemned as a crazy idea 把 craze 这个原词联想成「crazy／疯狂主意被谴责」。craze（风靡）和 crazy（疯狂）发音相近但意思相反，录音根本没有谴责之意，是听音近词就选的陷阱。 借用原文：bring new life into downtown
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：enriching the city's night life 听着像呼应录音里夜里、城市等词，但录音第 4 段说的是引进电动车是为了 bring new life into downtown（带来新活力，那是目的／初衷），并没说它正在丰富夜生活。把第 4 段的目的安到第 5 题的现状评价上，张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：questioned by local residents 里的「被本地居民质疑」在录音里找不到落点：报道讲的是 safety concerns（安全担忧），并没有出现 local residents 质疑这一方。属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（they're leading to safety concerns ↔ It is giving rise to safety concerns. lead to = give rise to）

questions.evidenceText: But they're leading to safety concerns, mainly at night when some riders don't follow the rules of the road.

questions.stem: What are electric bike riders supposed to do?

options.text: Follow all the traffic rules drivers do.
Give way to automobiles at all times.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile.信号：义务句 have to 即落点 。第 3 段 have to follow all the same rules 里的 have to（必须）是明确的义务标志。预读时就定了「听 have to／must」，这句一出现…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Avoid entering one-way streets 盗用了录音 one-way streets 这个原词，但录音说的是「不要在单行道上逆行（traveling in the opposite direction）」，不是「避免进入单行道」。它只截取了规则里的一个例子并改了意思，答非所问——题目问的是总要求，不是某一条细则。 借用原文：on pedestrian paths
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：Ensure the safety of pedestrians 里的 pedestrians 借自第 2 段 pedestrian paths。但录音从没要求骑车人「保证行人安全」；第 4 段只说骑车人和司机都要 paying attention（注意安全）。把注意夸成保证行人安全，且 pedestrian 一词出处也不对，张冠李戴。 借用原文：as you would if you were in an automobile
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：Give way to automobiles at all times 借了录音的 automobile 一词，但录音说骑车人要遵守「和开汽车一样的规则」，是平等守规，绝没有「随时给汽车让路」的意思。at all times（任何时候）是绝对化的无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile ↔ Follow all the traffic rules drivers do. in an automobile = drivers do）

questions.evidenceText: Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile.

questions.stem: Why did City Council member Anna Cumber advocate the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?

options.text: To ease the city's busy traffic.
To bring new life into the city.
To add a new means of transport.
To reduce the city's air pollution.

questions.analysis: 目的题。答案句（P4）：City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown.信号：目的状语 as a way to 。第 4 段 as a way to bring new life into downtown 里的 as a way to（作为……的一种方式）就是明确的目的标志，它后面接的就是 …

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：To ease the city's busy traffic 听着合理，但录音里 Anna Cumber 引进电动车的目的只说了 bring new life into downtown，从没提缓解繁忙交通。属无中生有的合理化推断。
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：To add a new means of transport 看似没错——电动车确实是新交通工具，但录音点明的目的是带来新活力，不是增加一种交通方式。这是顺着常识多推一步、偏离原文所说目的。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：To reduce the city's air pollution 引入「空气污染」这个全新概念，录音通篇没出现 pollution 或环保相关内容。属彻底的无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（as a way to bring new life into downtown ↔ To bring new life into the city. downtown = the city）

questions.evidenceText: City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown.

transcript.text: M: What's the best way to teach children how to save and spend their money?
transcript.zh: M: 教孩子如何存钱和花钱,最好的方法是什么?

transcript.text: W: You should make money a regular topic of discussion. It's best to start young, so it's instinctive rather than a scary subject.
transcript.zh: W: 你应该把钱的话题作为日常讨论的内容。最好从小开始,这样就会成为本能反应,而不是一个可怕的话题。

transcript.text: M: In our family, we talk openly about things like the budget for holidays, how taxes reduce your income, and how to shop around for the best deals.
transcript.zh: M: 在我们家,我们公开讨论像假期预算、税收如何减少你的收入,以及如何货比三家找到最优惠的价格这类事情。

transcript.text: W: Indeed. It's also essential to make money real for children through practical examples. Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums.
transcript.zh: W: 确实如此。通过实际例子让孩子对金钱有真实感受也很重要。比如算出使用披萨折扣券能省多少钱,这比抽象的数字计算要实用得多。

transcript.text: M: We also give our kids pocket money, and the amount they get is linked to chores, such as putting the bins out and emptying the dishwasher.
transcript.zh: M: 我们还给孩子零花钱,金额多少跟家务挂钩,比如倒垃圾和清空洗碗机。

transcript.text: W: We do that too, and it's paid according to their age. Two pounds for each year so they can see some progression.
transcript.zh: W: 我们也这样做,而且是按年龄支付。每岁两英镑,这样他们能看到一些进步。

transcript.text: M: Teaching them to save is important. We opened a savings account when they were young. After birthdays and Christmas, they would go to the branch and deposit their gift money.
transcript.zh: M: 教他们存钱很重要。我们在他们小时候就开了储蓄账户。生日和圣诞节过后,他们会去银行网点存入收到的礼金。

transcript.text: W: Oh, I hadn't considered doing that. In our house, we have transparent money boxes for them to put small change in, so they can see their savings grow.
transcript.zh: W: 哦,我还没考虑过这样做。在我们家,我们有透明的存钱罐让他们放零钱,这样他们能看到自己的储蓄增长。

transcript.text: M: When the time is right, I'll start talking to our children about investing and show them how the money saved for their further education has grown.
transcript.zh: M: 时机成熟时,我会开始跟孩子们谈投资,让他们看看为他们继续教育存的钱是如何增长的。

transcript.text: W: I am always talking to my elder daughter about the importance of saving into a pension. She's just started a part-time job and was thinking of not contributing to her pension. Luckily, I managed to persuade her otherwise.
transcript.zh: W: 我一直跟大女儿强调存养老金的重要性。她刚开始做兼职,本来想着不缴纳养老金。幸好我说服了她。

transcript.text: M: Yes, it's such an important lesson to learn.
transcript.zh: M: 是的,这是非常重要的一课。

questions.stem: What should we do with the topic of money, according to the woman?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：You should make money a regular topic of discussion.信号：应答方的 should 建议句 。男士问"最好怎么教孩子理财"，女士开口第一句就是 You should make money a regular topic of discussion，should 是明确的建议信…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：Take it seriously.（认真对待）听起来很顺理成章，但女士没说要"认真严肃对待"，反而强调要让它不吓人、变本能，属凭常识脑补、原文未提。
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：录音里女士说要让钱"不是个吓人的话题" rather than a scary subject，Make it sound scary. 盗用了原词 scary 却把意思反了过来，正是"听到原词就想选"的陷阱。 借用原文：we talk openly about things
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：Talk about it openly. 对应的 openly 来自男士的话 we talk openly about things，是男士说的，而题目问的是 according to the woman（女士），把男士的话安到女士头上，属张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a regular topic of discussion ↔ Discuss it regularly 名词短语改写成动词）

questions.evidenceText: You should make money a regular topic of discussion.

questions.stem: How does the woman say money can be made real for children?

options.text: By shopping around for the best deals.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：It's also essential to make money real for children through practical examples. Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums.信号：for example 引出具体做法 。女士说要 through practical examples 并紧接 for example 举出披萨折扣券的例子，practical examples 加 for exam…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：By shopping around for the best deals. 里 shopping around for the best deals 是男士在 how to shop around for the best deals 里说的别的话题，且非"让钱变真实"的方法，原词照搬却答非所问。 借用原文：much more relevant than abstract sums
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：录音说具体例子"比抽象算数有意义得多" much more relevant than abstract sums，abstract sums 是被否定、被比下去的一方；By making abstract sums relevant. 盗用这两个词反过来说"让抽象算数变得相关"，与原文相反。 借用原文：discount pizza coupons
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：By visiting discount stores. 里 discount 来自录音的 discount pizza coupons（折扣券），但原文是"用折扣券"不是"逛折扣店"，盗一个 discount 把概念偷换了。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（through practical examples ↔ By citing concrete examples 同义词替换）

questions.evidenceText: It's also essential to make money real for children through practical examples. Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums.

questions.stem: What is the common practice between the man and the woman?

options.text: Paying their kids to help with housework.
Setting kids a good example by sharing chores.

transcript.text: One thing that extreme sports do better than perhaps anything else is to help you stop being afraid. It may sound strange to say that their main function is to reduce fear. But after a time, your fear response to other things in life will be dramatically reduced. After all, if you can jump out of a plane or off a bridge, then you can face anything else easily.

transcript.text: When doing extreme sports, you have to become more focused. You'll be pushed to your limits, and if you aren't focused you'll make dangerous mistakes. Learning to be this focused when enjoying extreme sports will help you to be focused at work, keeping you more productive and ultimately more successful.
transcript.zh: 在进行极限运动时,你必须变得更加专注。你会被推向极限,如果不够专注就会犯下危险的错误。在享受极限运动时学会如此专注将帮助你在工作中保持专注,使你更高效,最终更成功。

transcript.text: It's great to stay fit and healthy, but standard exercise routines and sports only work the same muscles repeatedly. With extreme sports, you'll be working entirely different muscles, and that means you get an all-over workout. Extreme sports also burn a lot more calories than other sports. A team of researchers led by Priyanka Joshi examined the degree to which men and women relied on "communicative abstraction" to verbally convey their ideas and emotions. Interestingly, they found that men were far more likely to speak in the abstract than were women.

To arrive at this 28______ , the researchers examined the linguistic(语言的) patterns of men and women in over 600,000 blog posts written on websites. To do this, the researchers computed abstractness ratings for 29______ 40,000 commonly used words in the English language. Words considered to be concrete could be easily visualized, such as "table" or "chair". Words that were more 30______ to visualize, for example, "justice" or "morality" were considered to be more abstract. They found that men used 31______ more abstract language in their blog posts.

What is the 32______ of this effect? The researchers suggest that power differences between the genders—that is, men having more power in society—might be a key determinant(决定因素). For instance, in a follow-up study conducted with a sample of 300 students, the researchers 33______ power dynamics in an interpersonal setting to see if this would influence communicative abstraction. They found that participants in a high-power interviewer role were more likely to give abstract descriptions of behaviors than were participants in a low-power interviewee role. This suggests that communicating more abstractly does not reflect a 34______ tendency of men or women but rather 35______ within specific contexts.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Hal Hershfield, a psychologist at the UCLA Anderson School of Management, wanted to know why people weren't saving for retirement. Across the board, people are living longer. Logically, they'll need more money to live comfortably in their post-work years. And yet, savings rates in the U.S. have gone down in recent decades, not up.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: To help explain this seemingly irrational behavior, Hershfield and his team scanned the brains of study participants while asking them to what degree various traits(特征)—like "honorable" or "funny"—applied to their current self, their future self, a current other, or a future other. As participants answered, Hershfield's team recorded which parts of their brains lit up. Unsurprisingly, people's brains were most active when thinking about their current selves and least active when thinking about a current other. But the team found that participants' brain activity while considering their future selves more closely resembled their brain activity while thinking about a current other rather than the current self.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Put in practical terms, when thinking of yourself in a month or a year or a decade, your brain registers that person in ways similar to how it would register Taylor Swift or the mailman. Understood in that way, saving for retirement is the equivalent of giving money away to someone else entirely.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: In light of Hershfield's study, one simple question arises: Is it possible to make our present selves give a damn about our future selves? The answers are anything but simple.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Seen through the lens of the present self versus the future self, our self-defeating actions—like choosing to watch television rather than go to the gym—suddenly make perfect sense. We get to enjoy the very concrete, immediate benefits of our actions while someone else (namely, our future selves) suffers the hypothetical(假设的), far-off consequences. As a result, the decisions we make for our present selves often look very different from our decisions for our future selves. We believe that tomorrow will be different. We believe that we will be different tomorrow; but in doing so, we prioritize our current mood over the consequences of our inaction for the future self.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Understanding our procrastination(拖延) through the lens of the present and future selves, we're left with three possible solutions: The first is to force your future self to do whatever your present self doesn't want to do. The second is to convince your present self that your future self is, in fact, still you. If the central problem is that we think of our future selves as other people, it follows that trying to identify more closely with our future selves will encourage us to make better long-term decisions.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In a follow-up study, Hershfield wanted to explore ways to bridge the disconnect between the present and future selves and encourage people to save more for retirement. He and his team took photos of study participants, and then used image processing to visually age their faces. Participants were then placed in a virtual reality setting where they could look into a mirror and see their aged selves looking back at them. Participants who saw their aged selves said they would save 30% more of their salary for retirement than the control group.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Whatever your long-term goals may be—getting in better shape, launching your own business, writing a book—thinking about your deadline in terms of days rather than months or years can help you wrap your mind around how close the future really is.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: The third solution is to forget about your future self and use your present self's love of instant gratification(满足感) to your advantage. While the two tactics(手段) above can be effective in making better long-term choices, in the end, you're still struggling against human nature. Our brains are hard-wired for instant gratification. Instead of fighting your present self's need for immediate rewards, why not use it to your advantage? When most of us set goals, we focus on long-term results we want to see—e.g., losing weight, getting a promotion, retiring in comfort, etc. While those visions of our future selves can be inspiring, when it comes to actually doing the day-to-day work, it may be more effective to reframe activities in terms of their immediate, or at least very near-term, rewards.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Take writing this article, for instance. It's easy for me to imagine how amazing it will feel at the end of the workday to have this article done. This isn't just my opinion. Research partners Kaitlin Woolley of Cornell University and Ayelet Fishbach of the University of Chicago have made a career out of studying the differences between the goals that people achieve and the ones that fall to the wayside.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: "In one study, we asked people online about the goals they set at the beginning of the year. Most people set goals to achieve delayed, long-term benefits, such as career advancement, debt repayment, or improved health. We asked these individuals how enjoyable it was to pursue their goal, as well as how important their goal was. We also asked whether they were still working on their goals two months after setting them. We found that enjoyment predicted people's goal persistence two months after setting the goal far more than how important they rated their goal to be," Woolley said.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: This pattern held true across a wide variety of goals from exercising to studying to eating healthier foods. For example, people ate 50% more of a healthy food when directed to focus on the good taste rather than the long-term health benefits. Other studies have shown a greater uptake of exercise in people who were told to think of the enjoyment of doing the exercise now rather than future health gains.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: These findings suggest that when it comes to achieving your goals, enjoying the process itself is more important than wanting the long-term benefits. In other words, present self trumps(战胜) future self. Who says instant gratification has to be a bad thing? By all means, set ambitious long-term goals for your future self, but when it comes to actually following through day-to-day, make sure your present self knows what's in it for her too.
